q-146180.name: Question 1
q-146180.problem:
$$
{f}_{Y\,|\,X}(y\,|\,1)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1+{y}^{2}}{12}, & \,\,0\le y\le 3 \\ 0, & \,\,\text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Let $X$ and $Y$ be continuous random variables. 
Find the conditional expected value $\text{E}[Y\,|\,X=1]$ given that the conditional probability density function ${f}_{Y|X}(y\,|\,1)$ is shown above.
q-146180.worked_solution:
Recall that the conditional expected value of $Y$ given $X=x$ is defined by

$$
\text{E}[Y\,|\,X=x]={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }y\,{f}_{Y|X}(y\,|\,x)\,\text{d}y.
$$

Therefore, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[Y\,|\,X=1] & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }y\,{f}_{Y|X}(y\,|\,1)\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}y\cdot \frac{1+{y}^{2}}{12}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{1}{12}{\int }_{0}^{3}(y+{y}^{3})\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{1}{12}{[\frac{{y}^{2}}{2}+\frac{{y}^{4}}{4}]}_{0}^{3} \\  & =\frac{1}{48}(99-0) \\  & =\frac{33}{16}.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
{f}_{Y\,|\,X}(y\,|\,1)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{2+2y}{3}, & \,\,0\le y\le 1 \\ 0, & \,\,\text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Let $X$ and $Y$ be continuous random variables. 
Find the conditional expected value $\text{E}[Y\,|\,X=1]$ given that the conditional probability density function ${f}_{Y|X}(y\,|\,1)$ is shown above.
q-146188.worked_solution:
Recall that the conditional expected value of $Y$ given $X=x$ is defined by

$$
\text{E}[Y\,|\,X=x]={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }y\,{f}_{Y|X}(y\,|\,x)\,\text{d}y.
$$

Therefore, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[Y\,|\,X=1] & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }y\,{f}_{Y|X}(y\,|\,1)\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}y\cdot \frac{2+2y}{3}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{2}{3}{\int }_{0}^{1}(y+{y}^{2})\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{2}{3}{[\frac{{y}^{2}}{2}+\frac{{y}^{3}}{3}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =\frac{2}{3}(\frac{1}{2}+\frac{1}{3}-0) \\  & =\frac{5}{9}.\end{aligned}
$$

q-146177.name: Question 3
q-146177.problem:
$$
{f}_{X\,|\,Y}(x\,|\,3)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{3{x}^{2}}{8}, & \,\,0\le x\le 2 \\ 0, & \,\,\text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Let $X$ and $Y$ be continuous random variables. 
Find the conditional expected value $\text{E}[X\,|\,Y=3]$ given that the conditional probability density function ${f}_{X|Y}(x\,|\,3)$ is shown above.
q-146177.worked_solution:
Recall that the conditional expected value of $X$ given $Y=y$ is defined by

$$
\text{E}[X\,|\,Y=y]={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }x\,{f}_{X|Y}(x\,|\,y)\,\text{d}x.
$$

Therefore, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[X\,|\,Y=3] & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }x\,{f}_{X|Y}(x\,|\,3)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}x\cdot \frac{3{x}^{2}}{8}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}\frac{3{x}^{3}}{8}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={[\frac{3{x}^{4}}{32}]}_{0}^{2} \\  & =\frac{48}{32}-\frac{0}{32} \\  & =\frac{3}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

q-145631.problem:
$$
{f}_{X|Y}(x\,|\,2)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{x}{4}, & \,1\le x\le 3 \\ 0, & \,\text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

Let $X$ and $Y$ be continuous random variables. 
Find the conditional expected value $\text{E}[X\,|\,Y=2]$ given that the conditional probability density function ${f}_{X|Y}(x\,|\,2)$ is shown above.
q-145631.worked_solution:
Recall that the conditional expected value of $X$ given $Y=y$ is defined by

$$
\text{E}[X\,|\,Y=y]={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }x\,{f}_{X|Y}(x\,|\,y)\,\text{d}x.
$$

Therefore, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[X\,|\,Y=2] & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }x\,{f}_{X|Y}(x\,|\,2)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{3}x\cdot \frac{x}{4}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{3}\frac{{x}^{2}}{4}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={[\frac{{x}^{3}}{12}]}_{1}^{3} \\  & =\frac{27}{12}-\frac{1}{12} \\  & =\frac{13}{6}.\end{aligned}
$$

q-146253.name: Question 6
q-146253.problem:
$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{2x+3y}{12}, & 1\le x\le 2,\,0\le y\le 2, \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}\,{f}_{Y}(y)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{y+1}{4}, & 0\le y\le 2, \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Let $X$ and $Y$  be continuous random variables. Their joint probability density function and the marginal probability density function of $Y$ are shown above. Find the conditional expected value $\text{E}[X\,|\,Y=1].$
q-146253.worked_solution:
Recall that the conditional expected value of $X$ given $Y=y$ is defined by

$$
\text{E}[X\,|\,Y=y]={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }x\,{f}_{X|Y}(x\,|\,y)\,\text{d}x.
$$

Note that $\text{E}[X\,|\,Y=y]$ is a function of $y.$ 

The conditional density function of $X$ given $Y=y$ can be computed as 

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{X|Y}(x\,|\,y) & =\frac{f(x,y)}{{f}_{Y}(y)} \\  & =\frac{(\frac{2x+3y}{12})}{(\frac{y+1}{4})} \\  & =\frac{2x+3y}{3y+3},\end{aligned}
$$

where $1\le x\le 2,\,0\le y\le 2.$ Outside this domain, we have ${f}_{X|Y}(x\,|\,y)=0.$

Now, substituting $y=1$ into the expression for ${f}_{X|Y}(x\,|\,y),$ we get

$$
{f}_{X|Y}(x\,|\,1)=\frac{2x+3\cdot 1}{3\cdot 1+3}=\frac{2x+3}{6}.
$$

Therefore, using the definition of the conditional expectation above, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[X\,|\,Y=1] & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }x\,{f}_{X|Y}(x\,|\,1)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}x\cdot \frac{2x+3}{6}\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{6}{\int }_{1}^{2}(2{x}^{2}+3x)\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{6}{[\frac{2{x}^{3}}{3}+\frac{3{x}^{2}}{2}]}_{1}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{6}((\frac{16}{3}+6)-(\frac{2}{3}+\frac{3}{2})) \\  & =\frac{55}{36}.\end{aligned}
$$

q-146345.problem:
$$

Let $X$ and $Y$  be continuous random variables. Their joint probability density function and the marginal probability density function of $X$ are shown above. Find the conditional expected value $\text{E}[Y\,|\,X=1].$
q-146345.worked_solution:
Recall that the conditional expected value of $Y$ given $X=x$ is defined by

$$
\text{E}[Y\,|\,X=x]={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }y\,{f}_{Y|X}(y\,|\,x)\,\text{d}y.
$$

Note that $\text{E}[Y\,|\,X=x]$ is a function of $x.$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{Y|X}(y\,|\,x) & =\frac{f(x,y)}{{f}_{X}(x)} \\  & =\frac{12xy}{6{x}^{5}} \\  & =\frac{2y}{{x}^{4}},\end{aligned}
$$

 

where $0<x\le 1,\,0\le y\le {x}^{2}.$ Outside this domain, we have ${f}_{Y|X}(y\,|\,x)=0.$

Now, substituting $x=1$ into the expression for ${f}_{Y|X}(y\,|\,x),$ we get

$$
{f}_{Y|X}(y\,|1\,)=2y.
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[Y\,|\,X=1] & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }y\,{f}_{Y|X}(y\,|\,1)\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}y\cdot (2y)\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(2{y}^{2})\text{d}y \\  & ={[\frac{2{y}^{3}}{3}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =\frac{2}{3}.\end{aligned}

Let $X$ and $Y$  be continuous random variables. Their joint probability density function and the marginal probability density function of $Y$ are shown above. Find the conditional expected value $\text{E}[X\,|\,Y=1].$

Recall that the conditional expected value of $X$ given $Y=y$ is defined by

$$
\text{E}[X\,|\,Y=y]={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }x\,{f}_{X|Y}(x\,|\,y)\,\text{d}x.
$$

Note that $\text{E}[X\,|\,Y=y]$ is a function of $y.$ 

The conditional density function of $X$ given $Y=y$ can be computed as 

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{X|Y}(x\,|\,y) & =\frac{f(x,y)}{{f}_{Y}(y)} \\  & =\frac{(2-x-y)}{(\frac{3}{2}-y)} \\  & =\frac{4-2x-2y}{3-2y},\end{aligned}
$$

where $0\le x\le 1,\,0\le y\le 1.$ Outside this domain, we have ${f}_{X|Y}(x\,|\,y)=0.$

Now, substituting $y=1$ into the expression for ${f}_{X|Y}(x\,|\,y),$ we get

$$
{f}_{X|Y}(x\,|\,1)=\frac{4-2x-2\cdot 1}{3-2\cdot 1}=\frac{4-2x-2}{3-2}=2-2x.
$$

Therefore, using the definition of the conditional expectation above, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[X\,|\,Y=1] & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }x\,{f}_{X|Y}(x\,|\,1)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}x(2-2x)\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(2x-2{x}^{2})\text{d}x \\  & ={[{x}^{2}-\frac{2{x}^{3}}{3}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =(1-\frac{2}{3})-0 \\  & =\frac{1}{3}.\end{aligned}

\begin{aligned}f(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{3x{y}^{2}}{4}, & 0\le y\le 2,\,0<x<1 \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}\,{f}_{X}(x)=\{\begin{aligned}2x, & 0<x<1 \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}

Let $X$ and $Y$  be continuous random variables. Their joint probability density function and the marginal probability density function of $X$ are shown above. Find the expression for the conditional expected value $\text{E}[Y\,|\,X=x]$ for $0<x<1.$
q-146397.worked_solution:
Recall that the conditional expected value of $Y$ given $X=x$ is defined by

$$
\text{E}[Y\,|\,X=x]={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }y\,{f}_{Y|X}(y\,|\,x)\,\text{d}y.
$$

Note that $\text{E}[Y\,|\,X=x]$ is a function of $x.$ 

The conditional density function of $Y$ given $X=x$ can be computed as 

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{Y|X}(y\,|\,x) & =\frac{f(x,y)}{{f}_{X}(x)} \\  & =\frac{(\frac{3x{y}^{2}}{4})}{2x} \\  & =\frac{3{y}^{2}}{8},\end{aligned}
$$

where $0\le y\le 2,\,0<x<1.$ Outside this domain, we have ${f}_{Y|X}(y\,|\,x)=0.$ 

Therefore, using the definition of the conditional expectation above, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[Y\,|\,X=x] & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }y\,{f}_{Y|X}(y\,|\,x)\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}y\cdot \,\frac{3{y}^{2}}{8}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{3}{8}{\int }_{0}^{2}{y}^{3}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{3}{8}{[\frac{{y}^{4}}{4}]}_{0}^{2} \\  & =\frac{3}{8}[4-0] \\  & =\frac{3}{8}\cdot 4 \\  & =\frac{3}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

q-146538.problem:
$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{2(x+2y)}{3}, & \,0\le x\le 1,\,0\le y\le 1 \\ 0, & \,\text{otherwise}\end{aligned}\,{f}_{Y}(y)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1+4y}{3}, & 0\le y\le 1 \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Let $X$ and $Y$  be continuous random variables. Their joint probability density function and the marginal probability density function of $Y$ are shown above. Find the expression for the conditional expected value $\text{E}[X\,|\,Y=y]$ for $0\le y\le 1.$
q-146538.worked_solution:
Recall that the conditional expected value of $X$ given $Y=y$ is defined by

$$
\text{E}[X\,|\,Y=y]={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }x\,{f}_{X|Y}(x\,|\,y)\,\text{d}x.
$$

Note that $\text{E}[X\,|\,Y=y]$ is a function of $y.$ 

The conditional density function of $X$ given $X=x$ can be computed as 

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{X|Y}(x\,|\,y) & =\frac{f(x,y)}{{f}_{Y}(y)} \\  & =\frac{(\frac{2(x+2y)}{3})}{(\frac{1+4y}{3})} \\  & =\frac{2(x+2y)}{1+4y},\end{aligned}
$$

where $0\le x\le 1,\,0\le y\le 1.$ Outside this domain, we have ${f}_{Y|X}(y\,|\,x)=0.$ 

Therefore, using the definition of the conditional expectation above, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[X\,|\,Y=y] & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }x\,{f}_{X|Y}(x\,|\,y)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}x\cdot \,\frac{2(x+2y)}{1+4y}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{2}{1+4y}{\int }_{0}^{1}({x}^{2}+2yx)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{2}{1+4y}{[\frac{{x}^{3}}{3}+y{x}^{2}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =\frac{2}{1+4y}\cdot [\frac{1}{3}+y-0] \\  & =\frac{2}{1+4y}\cdot \frac{1+3y}{3} \\  & =\frac{2(1+3y)}{3(1+4y)}.\end{aligned}
$$

q-146520.name: Question 15
q-146520.problem:
$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{6{x}^{2}+6y}{5}, & \,0\le x\le 1,\,0<y<1 \\ 0, & \,\text{otherwise}\end{aligned}\,{f}_{Y}(y)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{6y+2}{5}, & 0\le y\le 1 \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Let $X$ and $Y$  be continuous random variables. Their joint probability density function and the marginal probability density function of $Y$ are shown above. Find the expression for the conditional expected value $\text{E}[X\,|\,Y=y]$ for $0<y<1.$
q-146520.worked_solution:
Recall that the conditional expected value of $X$ given $Y=y$ is defined by

$$
\text{E}[X\,|\,Y=y]={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }x\,{f}_{X|Y}(x\,|\,y)\,\text{d}x.
$$

Note that $\text{E}[X\,|\,Y=y]$ is a function of $y.$ 

The conditional density function of $X$ given $X=x$ can be computed as 

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{X|Y}(x\,|\,y) & =\frac{f(x,y)}{{f}_{Y}(y)} \\  & =\frac{(\frac{6{x}^{2}+6y}{5})}{(\frac{6y+2}{5})} \\  & =\frac{6{x}^{2}+6y}{6y+2},\end{aligned}
$$

where $0\le x\le 1,\,0\le y\le 1.$ Outside this domain, we have ${f}_{Y|X}(y\,|\,x)=0.$ 

Therefore, using the definition of the conditional expectation above, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[X\,|\,Y=y] & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }x\,{f}_{X|Y}(x\,|\,y)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}x\cdot \,\frac{6{x}^{2}+6y}{6y+2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{6}{6y+2}{\int }_{0}^{1}({x}^{3}+xy)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{6}{6y+2}{[\frac{{x}^{4}}{4}+\frac{{x}^{2}y}{2}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =\frac{6}{6y+2}[\frac{1}{4}+\frac{y}{2}-0] \\  & =\frac{6}{6y+2}\cdot \frac{1+2y}{4} \\  & =\frac{6}{2(3y+1)}\cdot \frac{(1+2y)}{4} \\  & =\frac{3(1+2y)}{4(3y+1)}.\end{aligned}
$$
